title: SLA-anchored rewind autoscaler: fast recovery and bounded overshoot
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Context: We need an autoscaling policy engine variant for Dedicated fleets that (1) prioritizes meeting per-tenant throughput SLAs, (2) recovers capacity quickly after transient load spikes, and (3) bounds overshoot to minimize cost. The current conservative slew-based scaler maintains stability but is slow to recover in sudden sustained traffic bursts, leading to sustained SLA misses. This ticket proposes an SLA-anchored "rewind" autoscaler: a hybrid controller that uses an SLA-proportional target, a short-term predictive recovery reservoir, and a bounded-rewind mechanism that can temporarily exceed committed headroom but automatically rewinds to committed levels with safety windows and cooldowns.
acceptance_criteria: New autoscaler implementation deployed on a canary Dedicated pool and exercised by synthetic load tests
Per-tenant 95th percentile throughput meets configured SLA target in 90% of 10m windows during sustained bursts (>5x baseline) in canary tests
Peak overshoot (fleet-level extra GPUs) is bounded by configurable limit (default 15%) and never exceeds hard cap during tests
Rewind path reduces allocated capacity back to committed levels within configured rewind_window without causing >5% increase in observed p95 latency across tenants
Operational metrics (scale events/s, rollback events, time-to-first-scale, overshoot-percent) are visible in Console dashboards and have threshold alerts
End-to-end integration tests for failure modes (control plane partition, worker GC, metric dropouts) pass in staging
notes: 2026-02-15: Ticket created after postmortem for spike event on 2026-02-10 — SLA misses lasted ~13m while conservative scaler ramped up. Assigned to Diego.

2026-02-18: Design review with Runtimes and SRE. Agreed hybrid approach: PID-like proportional term for SLA error, a model-based short-term demand predictor for burst recovery, and a rewind governor for safe deallocation. Action: spike-sim harness and design doc (Confluence) requested.

2026-02-24: Prototype algorithm implemented in autoscale-sim (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8251). Early sims show 3x faster time-to-target but 10-18% temporary overshoot depending on predictor aggressiveness.

2026-03-02: Trade-off discussion: aggressive predictors reduce SLA misses but increase cost and eviction churn. Decided on two-tier controls: soft_rewind_budget (default 15%) and hard_rewind_cap (default 25%). Added cooldown heuristics tied to p95 latency stabilization.

2026-03-07: SRE requested additional safety: add persistent headroom accounting per-tenant to avoid repeated rewinds causing billing confusion. Will expose headroom metrics per customer and audit logs for rewinds.

2026-03-10: Canary rollout plan drafted. Initial canary pools selected (dedicated-pool-canary-7). Dashboard panels and alerts wired (PR: github.com/redwood/console/pull/4105). Preparing k8s job for staged traffic soak.
risks: Predictive component may be miscalibrated for novel tenant traffic patterns -> temporary cost spikes
Control plane partition or metric blackout during aggressive recovery could trigger runaway scaling; mitigated by hard_rewind_cap and watchdog
Frequent rewinds might increase eviction thrash in worker pools if not coordinated with placement logic
Billing and customer surprise due to transient capacity above committed level — requires product communication and audit logging
rollout_plan: Step 0: Run extended sims with historical workload traces (2 weeks) and confirm overshoot percent under hard cap
Step 1: Deploy algorithm behind feature flag in staging, enable for internal test tenants only
Step 2: Canary deploy to dedicated-pool-canary-7 for 48h under synthetic sustained bursts and gradual increases
Step 3: Open canary to a small set of low-risk customers with opt-in billing preview and enable detailed headroom dashboards
Step 4: Gradual ramp to 50% of fleet with monitoring guardrails; automatic rollback if >3% of tenants observe >10% SLA regressions
Step 5: Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics and sign-off from SRE/Product
test_plan: Unit tests for controller math and edge cases (NaN, divide-by-zero, stale metrics)
Integration tests: metric blackout, delayed KV cache refill, and simulated control plane partition
Load tests: replay of three production tenant traffic profiles (spiky, ramping, sustained) with and without predictor enabled
Chaos tests: kill scale-controller leader and verify failover and no runaway allocations
E2E: verify Console metrics, audit trail for rewinds, and billing preview report
metrics: Tenant-level throughput SLO attainment (p95 throughput vs configured target) — primary
Time-to-target (time from violation detection to allocated capacity meeting target) — aim < 180s
Overshoot percent (extra capacity above committed) — median and 95th — soft_budget default 15% hard_cap 25%
Rewind time (time to reduce back to committed after stabilization) — target < 10m
Scale events per hour per pool — safety threshold to detect thrash
Eviction rate and placement failures post-rewind — should not increase >2x baseline
